title: Pre-computing Unused Lookup Tables at Startup
pattern: Loading, parsing, and caching massive dataset files into memory indexes at application startup.
why_bad: It severely increases application cold-start times and consumes massive amounts of RAM for data points that may never be queried during the runtime lifecycle. Memory that is idle is wasted [361, 373].
detection: Large static initializers or dynamic parse trees loaded inside application startup macros before the first query is received.
counterexample: Core lookup indices (such as database schemas or routing tables) that are guaranteed to be queried immediately on every single request. `Contextual`.
fix: Utilize standard on-demand database querying (like SQLite) or lazy load segments index by index using dynamic file seeking.
